question: The practical application of the Birds1 and Habitats2 Directives has evolved considerably through the case-law of the Court of Justice of the European Union. In Finland, recent interpretations have raised questions about the relationship between the protection of birds’ nests under the Birds Directive and the strict protection of breeding and resting sites under the Habitats Directive.
These interpretations may have significant practical implications for land use and forestry, as well as for legal certainty for landowners and operators. 1.

Will the Commission’s ongoing stress test assess whether the challenges arising from the interpretation and application of the Birds and Habitats Directives can be addressed through guidance alone, or whether targeted legislative amendments are needed?

How will the Commission ensure the effective protection of species while providing sufficient legal certainty and flexibility for land use and forestry, taking account of national and regional circumstances? Is this going to be addressed in the upcoming update of these directives?

Directive 2009/147/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 30 November 2009 on the conservation of wild birds, OJ L 20, 26.1.2010, p. 7, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2009/147/oj. 2 Council Directive 92/43/EEC of 21 May 1992 on the conservation of natural habitats and of wild fauna and flora, OJ L 206, 22.7.1992, p. 7, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/1992/43/oj. 1
